title: Chainlink oracle ignores answeredInRound and has no min/max price bounds

location.code_snippet: try priceAggregator.latestRoundData() returns (uint80 roundId, int256 answer, uint256, uint256 timestamp, uint80 /* answeredInRound */) { if (roundId == 0) return 0; ... }

description: LibChainlinkOracle validates latestRoundData only via roundId!=0 and checkForInvalidTimestampOrAnswer (timestamp non-zero/not-future, within maxTimeout, answer>0). It never checks `answeredInRound >= roundId`, so a carried-over/stale answer from a prior round that still satisfies the timeout passes as fresh. It also applies no min/max sanity bounds on the returned answer, so during a Chainlink mispricing or a feed pinned at its circuit-breaker min/max the out-of-range value is consumed at face value (the protocol has no minAnswer/maxAnswer rejection). Heartbeat handling is coarse: FOUR_HOUR_TIMEOUT (14400s) is applied to feeds the comments describe as 1-hour heartbeat, accepting answers up to 4h stale.
impact: Stale (carried) Chainlink rounds within the 4h timeout and out-of-band circuit-breaker prices are accepted without rejection, feeding slightly-wrong USD prices into pricing/ratio math. Lower severity because Chainlink is the trusted source, the 0-on-failure design already handles outright outages, and the timeout bounds gross staleness.

ite.intent: Reject stale or out-of-range Chainlink answers so only fresh, sane prices are used.
ite.technique: answeredInRound is decoded but discarded; no min/max bound; coarse 4h timeout.
ite.evasion: The presence of roundId!=0 + timeout + answer>0 checks gives the appearance of full staleness validation while answeredInRound and bounds are missing.

ice_chain.corrupted_state: answer accepted as fresh/in-range without answeredInRound or min/max checks
ice_chain.consumer_action: slightly-wrong USD price consumed in ratio/pricing math
